text:
Drew Helleson spent early November at the center of a league-wide argument. His hit that sent Connor McDavid into the Ducks' net on Nov 5 went unpenalized, Vasily Podkolzin fought him and was given what The Athletic's Julian McKenzie described as a penalty for a "one-man fight", and The New York Times headlined McDavid "fuming" with the quote "I've got feelings and emotions too". The Hockey News asked whether McDavid overreacted.

Since then Anaheim has kept leaning on him. He's averaged 20.31 minutes over his last ten games, a jump of more than 3 minutes a night, including 24.3 against Pittsburgh. He has 2 assists in 13 games, and the Ducks have scored 4.85 fewer goals than their chances deserved with him on, which usually swings back. The five-on-five share isn't great (41.7% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, about 4 points worse than without him). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking gives reasons for patience: 56% of his exits kept possession last season, and his rate of passes that set up shots was in the 89th percentile among defensemen.
headline: Helleson's minutes are rising after the McDavid storm
